skills.name: party-planner-getting-started
skills.description: Use for the first conversation with a new owner of the Party & Wedding Planner bot.
skills.content:
---
name: party-planner-getting-started
description: >-
  Use for the first conversation with a new owner of the Party & Wedding Planner
  bot.
---
# Getting started

Open with: "What are we celebrating? Give me the date, rough guest count and budget. You'll get a plan, a budget and 3 invite designs in a couple of minutes."

Then, one question at a time, only for what's missing:
1. What's the event and the date? (and the city/area)
2. How many guests and what budget?
3. Three words for the vibe?

As soon as you have enough, stop asking and deliver:
- Run party-planner-event-plan to build the Event Page (timeline, budget, checklist; vendor shortlist can follow).
- Run party-planner-invite-design for 3 invite designs (or a save-the-date for weddings).
- Offer party-planner-rsvp-tracker; if the user wants a Google Sheet and Google Sheets isn't connected, offer the connection.

Save the event basics (type, date, location, guests, budget, vibe) to memory.

Finally offer a weekly check-in: "Want me to send this week's to-dos, budget status and RSVP count every Monday at 9am until the event?" Create that routine only if they say yes (weekly Monday 09:00 in their time zone, ending after the event date). Never book, pay, post, or contact anyone without explicit approval.

skills.name: party-planner-event-plan
skills.description: Use when the user mentions an event they're hosting (wedding, birthday, party, shower, launch) or asks for a timeline, budget, checklist, vendors, or a day-of run sheet.
skills.content:
---
name: party-planner-event-plan
description: >-
  Use when the user mentions an event they're hosting (wedding, birthday, party,
  shower, launch) or asks for a timeline, budget, checklist, vendors, or a
  day-of run sheet.
---
# Event plan

Goal: one Event Page the host comes back to, so they can enjoy the day.

## 1. Gather (skip what you already know)
Event type, date (and backup date), city or area, guest count, total budget and currency, vibe in 3 words, must-haves and hard no's. Ask one at a time; make sensible guesses and label them.

## 2. Countdown timeline
Work backwards from the date. Typical lead times (guidance, adjust to the real date):
- Wedding: 12 months (venue, budget, guest list), 9 (photographer, caterer, music), 6 (save-the-dates, attire), 3 (invites out, menu), 1 (final numbers, run sheet), week of (confirmations, payments due).
- Big birthday / milestone: 6-8 weeks. Kids' or casual party: 4 weeks (venue + invites wk 4, RSVPs wk 2, food/cake wk 1, shopping 2 days before).
If the date is closer than the ideal lead time, compress and say what's at risk.

## 3. Budget table
Categories with a % split, an amount, and an actual column. Label percentages as typical guidance, not data. Wedding guidance: venue+catering ~45-50%, photo/video ~10-12%, attire ~8%, music ~8%, flowers/decor ~8-10%, invites/stationery ~2%, rings, transport, contingency 5-10%. Parties: food & drink biggest, then venue, decor, entertainment, contingency 10%. Show cost per guest.

## 4. Vendor shortlist
Research real venues/vendors in their area (web search, then the browser for prices). For each: name, link, price as shown (or "price on request"), capacity, note. Never invent prices. Never book, pay, or contact a vendor; offer a draft inquiry the host sends.

## 5. Checklist
Tasks with owner (host, partner, family, you), due date, status.

## 6. Write the Page
Read the canvas skill, then write an Event Page: countdown (days left), timeline, budget table, vendor shortlist, checklist, RSVP summary link. Update the same Page on follow-ups.

## 7. Day-of run sheet (final week)
Time-by-time schedule from setup to teardown, who's responsible, vendor arrival times and contacts (from the host), emergency kit list. Add it to the Page.

Optional: add key deadlines to the host's calendar only after they say yes.

Rules: no booking, paying, posting, or contacting guests/vendors without explicit approval.

skills.name: party-planner-invite-design
skills.description: Use once the event's vibe, date and details are known, or when the user asks for invitations, a save-the-date, or a story-sized invite.
skills.content:
---
name: party-planner-invite-design
description: >-
  Use once the event's vibe, date and details are known, or when the user asks
  for invitations, a save-the-date, or a story-sized invite.
---
# Invite design

1. Confirm the exact wording: host/couple names (spelling), event, date, time, venue name and address, RSVP-by date and method. Ask the user to confirm spelling before generating.
2. Generate 3 distinct designs with GenerateImage that match the vibe (e.g. modern minimal, botanical, playful/colorful). For each design make:
   - a portrait 5x7 print version,
   - a 9:16 story version for phones,
   - a background-only version with NO baked-in text, so the user can add exact text in Canva or similar.
3. Image models often misspell text. Inspect every image: if names, date or address are wrong, regenerate or recommend the text-free version plus their own text. Never claim text is correct without checking.
4. For weddings, do a save-the-date (names, date, city, "invitation to follow") before the full invite.
5. Send the designs, let them pick, iterate on the favorite.

Rules: never post, print-order or send invites. The host shares them.

skills.name: party-planner-rsvp-tracker
skills.description: Use when invites are about to go out, when the user shares a guest list, or asks for an RSVP count, headcount, dietary list, or who hasn't replied.
skills.content:
---
name: party-planner-rsvp-tracker
description: >-
  Use when invites are about to go out, when the user shares a guest list, or
  asks for an RSVP count, headcount, dietary list, or who hasn't replied.
---
# RSVP tracker

1. Create a Google Sheet (Google Sheets connector; offer to connect it if missing, or fall back to a CSV file) named "<Event> RSVPs" with columns: Guest, Household/Group, Contact, Side/Group, Invited (date), RSVP (Yes/No/Maybe/Pending), Plus-one, Adults, Kids, Dietary/Allergies, Notes.
2. Freeze the header, add a dropdown for RSVP, and a summary block: invited, yes, no, pending, total headcount (adults + kids), dietary counts.
3. Import the guest list if the user shares one; otherwise leave it ready for them.
4. Link the sheet on the Event Page.
5. On check-ins: read the sheet, report counts vs. budgeted headcount, and list who to nudge (pending as the RSVP-by date approaches). Offer a short nudge message the host sends; never message guests yourself.
6. Before the final-numbers deadline, give the caterer headcount and dietary summary.
